verdicts.title: Make is_instance_of_union element checks real: handle empty iterables, check all elements, support Literal
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically: before-snippets verbatim, all claimed before/after behaviors reproduce exactly on all three backends ([] in bv -> True everywhere, ['x'] in bv -> False everywhere, generator inputs preserved, Literal branch works, ValueError branch for multi-arg generics intact), full suite 854 passed after this patch alone, and all call-site categories checked (three BitVector impls' __contains__/startswith/endswith/count, bittypes/int.py to_pyint, ctypes_ gate, legacy+dispatcher UnitType gates -- the aggregate/ctypes unions contain no Iterable arm, so oracle and dispatcher move together via the one shared helper; fastpath parity unaffected; BitsCastable confirmed @runtime_checkable in all three impls so the newly-reachable union arms are isinstance-safe). One quantified caveat the risk note understates: the gate on large plain-list inputs goes O(1)->O(n) with a heavy constant (~2.7us/element -- two caught TypeErrors per element recursing through Union[Literal[0,1],int]); measured `([0,1]*200000) in bv`: 0.0016s before -> 0.55s after (~340x for the whole operation, gate-dominated). Complexity class is unchanged as claimed and no in-package or benchmark hot path passes large plain lists (str/BitVector/bitarray inputs hit O(1) union arms first), so this is a user-convenience-path constant-factor regression only; a cheap isinstance(element, int) fast path before the recursive per-element check would remove most of it. Nit: is_instance_of_union(True, Literal[0,1]) returns True via int equality (True==1).

verdicts.title: Sync the is_array=True list-return fix into the frozen oracle's from_bytes_aggregate
verdicts.issues: Structurally and empirically verified: before-snippets verbatim (docstring + body); after the patch, oracle==dispatcher parity holds on every case probed, including cases the proposal did not mention: empty buffer ([] == []; oracle previously raised TypeError for missing dataclass args), non-multiple-length buffers for dataclass and scalar (both sides raise ValueError), nested dataclass arrays, and byte-identical non-array paths (146 plan_fastpath differential tests pass). The dispatcher never delegates with is_array=True (aggregate_types.py:229-244), so nothing else observes the oracle change; grep confirms no other in-package caller of the oracle's is_array. The extended parity test genuinely pins the sync: against the pristine oracle it fails (single nested record, and ValueError on the scalar case). Full suite 854/865 green with patch and test extension. Two prose errors in the proposal, neither affecting the fix: (1) the verified claim says 'all 160 plan_fastpath differential tests pass' -- the file has 146 (all pass); (2) the risks note claims that with S2 applied, unsupported entry types in the array path 'fail with the clear TypeError from count_bits' -- actually they fail earlier in count_bits_in_aggregate_type via dataclasses.fields with 'must be called with a dataclass type or instance' (verified; identical through both entry points, so parity still holds).

verdicts.title: Raise TypeError from count_bits_in_unit_type for unsupported types instead of returning None
verdicts.issues: Verified: before-snippet verbatim; the oracle-sync claim is structurally correct and empirically confirmed -- conversions/aggregate_types.count_bits_in_unit_type is a cache wrapper over _orig_count_bits_in_unit_type = _legacy.count_bits_in_unit_type (aggregate_types.py:66,111), the wrapper's try/except only guards the cache dict lookup, so the new TypeError propagates from all three entry points (legacy, cached public, count_bytes arithmetic caller) with the clear message, and a repeat call still raises (failures never cached -- an improvement over before, where the public wrapper cached the None). _legacy.count_bits_in_unit_type is also rebound to the wrapper (line 132), so oracle-internal recursion raises identically, e.g. a dataclass with one bad field type now names the offending type. Happy paths (CType/BitType/PyType/dataclass) unchanged; grep confirms no caller branches on a None return anywhere in the package. Full suite green; the paired test passes through all three asserted entry points. No issues.

verdicts.title: Make to_bytes_aggregate raise on unconvertible input like its to_bits_aggregate dual
verdicts.issues: Verified: before-snippet verbatim; single-oracle-edit-fixes-both confirmed structurally (public to_bytes_aggregate only short-circuits plan-eligible dataclass instances at aggregate_types.py:192-198 and delegates everything else, including all fall-through inputs, to _legacy.to_bytes_aggregate) and empirically (TypeError with the mirrored 'to bytes' message raised through BOTH entry points for NotConvertible() and None). No over-raising: [] -> b'', zero-field dataclass -> b'', {} (empty dict, Iterable branch) -> b'', 'a' -> b'a', normal dataclasses unchanged. Message mirrors to_bits_aggregate verbatim modulo bits->bytes as claimed. Full suite green including plan_fastpath differentials. Pre-existing quirks intentionally untouched and worth knowing, not blocking: passing a dataclass CLASS (not instance) still enters the DataClassType branch (is_dataclass is true for classes) and dies later with AttributeError, and the to_bits str-length>1 carve-out asymmetry remains -- both outside this finding's scope.

verdicts.title: Fix twos_complement docstring: phantom 'bits' param, convert to the file's Google-style Args/Returns
verdicts.issues: Verified: before-snippet verbatim at utils.py:314-321; the file's actual convention is Google-style Args:/Returns: (is_instance_of_union, is_subclass_of_union, twos_complement_bit_length all use it; twos_complement was the lone RST field-list holdout), so the conversion matches the house style rule for this reference-era file. Behavior pins check out: twos_complement(5, n_bits=8) == '00000101', twos_complement(-3, n_bits=4) == '1101', bits=8 raises TypeError as documented. Returns description ('str of the two's-complement bits') is accurate. Docstring-only; suite unaffected. No issues.
